settings.kill_roas_threshold: pause if ROAS < 1.0x after ₹500 spend on a sales-objective campaign
settings.reactivate_min_historic_roas: surface for reactivation if a paused campaign's last active-period ROAS >= 3.0x
settings.budget_reallocation_min_roas_gap: shift budget when one active campaign's ROAS is 1.5x+ another's
settings.note: hard_spend_ceiling_inr is a placeholder — set to roughly 3x trailing-30-day avg daily spend (~₹663/day as of 29 Aug 2026). All fields here are editable directly in the Automation tab (Save button) or by telling Claude.

proposals.actionSummary: Reactivate campaign 'Kage_Sales' (id 120255012429830159) with a conservative starting daily budget (≈₹200–300/day, versus its historical pace) and monitor for 3 days before scaling further.

proposals.title: Launch a Dynamic Product Ads (DPA) campaign from the connected Shopify catalog
proposals.reasoning: A Shopify product catalog is already connected to this ad account (catalog_id 1149969713295773), but zero DPA/catalog-based campaigns are currently running. Gully Labs (main competitor) runs DCO/catalog ads as part of their active mix; KAI runs none. This is a structural gap, not a performance one. Meta's own Opportunity Score tool (account score 85/100 as of 2026-08-29, down from 88) still flags Advantage+ catalog ads as a top recommendation (+4 points, 'lower cost per action'). Catalog health check re-run on 2026-08-29 found the same 3 diagnostic issues, one improved: 18 items still marked out-of-stock (must_fix — these won't appear in dynamic ads, unchanged), 24 items with fewer than 2 images (opportunity, unchanged), and only 1 unmatched content ID between the catalog and pixel now (opportunity, down from 4).
proposals.actionSummary: Fix the 18 out-of-stock catalog items first (update availability), check catalog health (ads_catalog_get_diagnostics), create a product set for best-sellers, and launch a catalog sales (DPA) campaign targeting site visitors/past purchasers.

params.note: start with a best-sellers product set before a full-catalog campaign; confirm out-of-stock items are resolved first
catalog-based dynamic ad against the new product set

proposals.title: Exclude existing purchasers from Kage_sales_1908 prospecting targeting
proposals.reasoning: Kage_sales_1908 is the account's only active sales-objective prospecting campaign (₹5,089.63 spent in the last 30 days, ROAS 1.57x — down from 1.84x on 2026-08-28's smaller spend base). Its ad set (id 120255351569140159) targets broad interest/behavior segments (Footwear, Sneakers, Street fashion, Frequent Travelers, Engaged Shoppers) with Advantage+ audience expansion on, but the targeting spec still has no excluded_custom_audiences entry — re-checked directly against the live targeting spec on 2026-08-29. A re-check of the account's custom audiences on 2026-08-29 found an existing 'Purchasers 30D' audience (id 120249907176770159, subtype PLATFORM/website pixel-based, delivery_status ACTIVE) that was not previously known — no need to create a new audience, it can be applied directly. Some fraction of prospecting spend is likely re-reaching people who already bought, which understates true new-customer efficiency.
proposals.actionSummary: Add the existing 'Purchasers 30D' custom audience (id 120249907176770159) as an excluded audience on Kage_sales_1908's ad set targeting, leaving all other targeting unchanged. No new audience needs to be created.

params.note: add existing custom audience id 120249907176770159 ('Purchasers 30D') to excluded_custom_audiences in the existing targeting spec; do not otherwise modify targeting

proposals.title: Exclude WhatsApp placement from Kage_sales_1908
proposals.reasoning: 30d placement breakdown for Kage_sales_1908 (the account's only active sales campaign): the 'whatsapp_marketing_messages' placement spent ₹262.34 on 195 impressions with 0 attributed purchases, at a CPM of ₹1,345.33 — roughly 11x the campaign's android_smartphone CPM (₹117.96) and 8x its iPhone CPM (₹160.51). This same spend shows up identically in the device breakdown as the 'other' impression_device bucket (₹262.34, CPM ₹1,345.33, 0 purchases) — same underlying placement, two views of the same number, not a separate issue. ₹262.34 is ~5.2% of the campaign's ₹5,089.64 30d spend going to a placement with zero conversions at a wildly elevated CPM. By contrast, this campaign's two dominant placements — instagram_reels (₹2,217.98, 1 purchase, 1.13x ROAS) and instagram_stories (₹780.12, 2 purchases, 7.01x ROAS) — are both converting, so this isn't a whole-campaign problem, just this one placement.
proposals.actionSummary: Remove 'whatsapp' from Kage_sales_1908's ad set targeting.publisher_platforms (keep facebook, instagram, audience_network, threads as-is). Note: Meta's targeting spec is inclusion-based (no separate excluded_publisher_platforms field), so this is applied by narrowing the publisher_platforms list rather than adding an exclusion.

params.note: remove 'whatsapp' from the existing targeting.publisher_platforms list; leave every other targeting parameter (including the purchaser exclusion from A-004, if already applied) unchanged

alerts.detail: Traffic-objective campaign, not sales-optimized, so 0 purchases is expected — not a kill signal on its own. As of 2026-08-29: frequency (1.04, trailing 7d) is still healthy, no fatigue. CTR has softened to 1.65% (trailing 7d) from 2.20% previously — worth watching but not yet a trigger on its own. Flagging so it stays on your radar if it doesn't start feeding a retargeting/conversion campaign soon.

alerts.title: 126 total campaigns on the account, 2 active
alerts.detail: The account has a long tail of old paused/dead campaigns (Black Friday, Diwali, and other one-off pushes going back over a year). Not urgent, but worth an archive/cleanup pass — a fragmented account history makes some of Meta's own learning-phase and benchmark signals less reliable.

alerts.title: Geo scaling/suppression can't run yet — Meta doesn't return purchase attribution at region level
alerts.detail: Checked the 30d region breakdown for both active campaigns. Kage_sales_1908 (the only sales campaign) has real spend concentration — Maharashtra ₹1,985.20 (2.16% CTR), Karnataka ₹902.39 (2.33% CTR), Telangana ₹584.60, Delhi ₹543.81 — but every single region row came back with omni_purchase/purchase_roas = null. This isn't a spend-volume problem (Maharashtra alone clears any reasonable meaningful-spend bar); it's the same Meta API limitation already disclosed on the dashboard's Geography tab (purchase attribution isn't returned cross-tabbed with region breakdowns). geo-scaling, geo-suppression, and new-geo-testing can only run on a CTR proxy until that changes, so skipped this run rather than propose budget moves off a proxy metric alone. Re-evaluate once spend is high enough to justify the same CTR-relative-ROAS estimation methodology the dashboard already uses for this tab.
